artifacts.summary: Confirms the hook's activation-detection precondition structurally cannot reach an orphaned (deleted/moved) project path; recommends a new --reap mode on setup-sapience-mcp.sh, invoked unconditionally by the SessionStart hook on every session (not gated on the current repo's own activation), touching only the sapience subkey; records the rejected alternatives (inline-hook edit, promoting verify-sapience-mcp.sh to a fixer) and the test cases to add.

memory_candidates.content: Sapience per-project MCP registration (setup-sapience-mcp.sh / sapience-mcp-register-project.sh) has a structural blind spot: the SessionStart hook's bidirectional register/remove logic is gated on finding a reachable .claude-extensions.json at the CURRENT session's CWD/git root, so a project whose directory is deleted or renamed can never again trigger its own entry's removal from ~/.claude.json -- the fix must be a cross-project sweep triggered from ANY still-living session, not a per-repo check.

In this codebase's MCP registration triads (sapience, lean-lsp), the writer script (e.g. setup-sapience-mcp.sh) is the single choke point for every ~/.claude.json mutation (mktemp + whole-file jq + mv); the SessionStart hook never edits the file directly, only decides which writer invocation to make. Any new mutation capability (e.g. an orphan-reap sweep) belongs as a new mode on the writer, not inlined in the hook.
